title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for depression.

HPI
Pt is an 80 y.o. female presenting for follow-up of major depressive disorder, single episode. Pt reports ongoing low mood and decreased interest in daily activities over the last month. She describes feelings of sadness and fatigue most days. Pt states she is having some difficulty with concentration but is still able to perform ADLs. No acute physical complaints reported today. Pt reports compliance with current medication regimen.

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Fatigue, positive.
Neuro: No tremors, no memory loss.
Psych: Low mood, positive.
Other: Negative.

Social History
Pt lives at home with her spouse. Retired. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Medication List
Sertraline 50mg PO daily
Multivitamin daily

Vitals
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Ht: 12.4
WBC: 7.2
Glucose: 104

Exam
General: Pt appears well-groomed, alert, and oriented x3. Affect is somewhat flat but congruent with mood. Speech is normal rate and volume. Mood is described as "down." Psychomotor activity is normal. Gait is steady. CTAB.

Assessment
1. Major depressive disorder, single episode. Current episode is moderate in severity.

Plan
1. Continue current dose of Sertraline. Pt to continue monitoring mood.
2. Follow up in 4 weeks for reassessment of symptoms.
3. Encouraged continued engagement in social activities and light exercise.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate (HCC 155): F32.1.

distractors.why: The provider documents moderate (HCC 155); mild has no HCC.
Severity is documented: do not use the unspecified code.
